gloss: bearing fruit; fruition; coming to fruition

definitions.explanation: The process of a plant producing fruit.
Efforts, plans, or work producing successful results. Used figuratively to describe when sustained effort finally pays off.

examples.japanese: りんごの{木|き}が{結実|けつじつ}した。
{受粉|じゅふん}しないと{結実|けつじつ}しない{品種|ひんしゅ}もある。
examples.english: Some varieties won't bear fruit without pollination.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}は{暖|あたた}かかったので{結実|けつじつ}が{早|はや}かった。
examples.english: It was warm this year, so the fruit set early.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{努力|どりょく}が{結実|けつじつ}した。
{研究|けんきゅう}がようやく{結実|けつじつ}して、{新薬|しんやく}が{完成|かんせい}した。
examples.english: The research finally came to fruition, and the new medicine was completed.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}の{交渉|こうしょう}が{結実|けつじつ}し、{条約|じょうやく}が{締結|ていけつ}された。
examples.english: The negotiations between the two countries bore fruit, and a treaty was concluded.

notes:
USAGE:
{結実|けつじつ} is used both literally for plants bearing fruit and figuratively for efforts producing results. The figurative sense is very common in writing and formal speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {努力|どりょく}が{結実|けつじつ}する (efforts bear fruit)
- {研究|けんきゅう}が{結実|けつじつ}する (research comes to fruition)
- {結実|けつじつ}を{見|み}る (to see results)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{実|みの}る also means "to bear fruit" (both literally and figuratively) but is native Japanese ({和語|わご}) and sounds more natural in everyday speech. {結実|けつじつ} is Sino-Japanese and more formal.
